transcript.text: Alright, let's get this release-readiness meeting started. We've got the proposal to publish our internal developer CLI to the public code repository next week, and before I make a final decision, I want to hear from each of your areas. Let's go through the standard reviews — developer tools, security, developer relations, and engineering operations. Who'd like to kick things off?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Before we go any further, I need to raise a serious blocker. While preparing the packaging script yesterday, I found that the repository bundles a parser library under the AGPL-3.0 license. Under our company's approved open-source terms, we cannot distribute AGPL-3.0-licensed code in this project. I hadn't filed the packaging issue yet because I was waiting to confirm the library's embedded version, but given that we're discussing a public release next week, we need to resolve this before any approval.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to raise a security blocker as well. This morning I inspected a runtime trace of the CLI and confirmed that it sends repository names and branch names to our company's hosted telemetry endpoint. Our policy for public distribution requires telemetry to be off by default, but the standard security scan that ran on the release did not exercise that runtime path, so this issue wasn't caught by the automated checks. I haven't added this finding to the release ticket yet, but it needs to be resolved before we can approve public publication.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a finding from my partner review that needs to be on the table. I checked the partner-access list during another review and found that the Northstar SSO plugin and the Kestrel billing plugin are proprietary extensions currently used by external pilot teams. Both of these plugin packages must be excluded from the public repository. The core CLI can still be published, but the current release draft proposes publishing the complete current repository, which would include these proprietary plugins. I have not yet updated the release draft to reflect this exclusion.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to raise an engineering operations blocker. While preparing next month's staffing report, I confirmed that our current ownership roster has no maintained support rotation for this project as a public offering. Our operations policy requires exactly two named maintainers and a recurring triage commitment before an internal tool can be published externally. That roster gap hasn't been raised in the release channel yet, but it needs to be resolved before we can approve public publication.
transcript.speaker: A5

transcript.text:
Thank you all for raising these findings. Let me make sure I have a clear picture of the four blockers before I record a decision:

1. Ravi — AGPL-3.0 licensed parser library bundled in the repository, which violates our approved open-source terms for distribution.
2. Elise — Telemetry sends repository names and branch names to our hosted endpoint, and our policy requires telemetry to be off by default for public distribution. The standard security scan didn't catch this because it didn't exercise that runtime path.
3. Jonah — The Northstar SSO plugin and the Kestrel billing plugin are proprietary extensions used by external pilot teams, and the current release draft would publish the complete repository including these.
4. Tessa — No maintained support rotation exists for this project as a public offering, and our operations policy requires exactly two named maintainers and a recurring triage commitment before external publication.

All four of these are legitimate blockers that need to be resolved before we can proceed. I will not approve the public release as currently proposed. However, I want to confirm with each of you: are there any additional findings from your areas beyond what you've just raised, or is this the complete set? I want to make sure we have everything on the table before I settle the plan.
